Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old man with several months of low mood, decreased appetite and energy, ~1-stone weight loss over ~6 months, intermittent nausea and headaches, and episodic palpitations/shortness of breath (not associated with chest pain) presenting for evaluation; plan to obtain baseline blood tests and arrange follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Low mood, reduced appetite, low energy ("feeling down", "out of place") for months.
  - Intermittent shortness of breath and palpitations, most notable in lifts/when standing in enclosed spaces.
  - Nausea intermittently when attempting to eat.
  - Headaches intermittently.
  - Weight loss of approximately one stone over ~6 months.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Mood/energy/appetite symptoms noted to have started after changing to a new law firm; patient estimates ~3–3.5 months for appetite change but weight loss began earlier (~6 months).
  - Patient stopped taking thyroxine around the time he changed doctors (timing coincides with symptom onset per patient).
  - Symptoms are chronic and have persisted/worsened enough to prompt contact.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Palpitations / shortness of breath occur repeatedly and are particularly pronounced in lifts; occurs "every time" in lifts. No clear exertional shortness of breath when walking (can walk ~1 mile without dyspnea, per patient).
  - No specific food triggers for nausea identified.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems (as mentioned):
  - Gastrointestinal: decreased appetite, intermittent nausea; no vomiting; bowel movements described as normal and painless; no diarrhea, blood, or mucus.
  - Cardiovascular/respiratory: episodic palpitations and sensation of not being able to breathe in lifts; no chest pain reported; no cough.
  - Neurologic: intermittent headaches.
  - Constitutional: unintentional weight loss (~1 stone).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No chest pain.
  - No cough.
  - No vomiting.
  - No diarrhea, no blood in stool.
  - No reported recent blood tests.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (described as "too little activity of my thyroid").
  - Patient previously took thyroxine.
  - Patient stopped taking thyroxine since changing doctors; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other chronic medical conditions were reported.
- No allergies were reported in the consult.

Medications:
- Thyroxine — patient states he previously took it but has not taken it since changing doctor; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other medications were mentioned.

Social History:
- Age: 35-year-old male.
- Occupation: Lawyer; reports some work-related stress after changing law firm.
- Living situation: married (wife mentioned); wife noted changes in "nightly activities" (context: decreased appetite/energy).
- Exercise: Patient states he "hasn't been walking lately" and reduced activity due to not feeling well.
- Tobacco / alcohol / recreational drug use: not discussed / not documented.
- Financial or housing concerns: not discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed / not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Vitals: not recorded / not provided.

Investigations:
- No investigations or lab results available at time of consult.
- Plan discussed to obtain a "general set of bloods" to look for:
  - Anaemia (CBC/hemoglobin) — mentioned.
  - Renal function — mentioned.
  - Liver function — mentioned.
  - Vitamin levels — mentioned.
  - Thyroid function tests were discussed conceptually given history of hypothyroidism (patient had not had blood tests in a long time); inclusion in blood testing plan is implied but not precisely specified in the transcript.
- No imaging or ECGs were performed or ordered on the call (not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Prolonged low mood, decreased appetite, low energy, unintentional weight loss
  - Assessment: Chronic low mood/anergia with decreased appetite and ~1-stone weight loss over ~6 months. Symptoms began or worsened after change of job and coincide with stopping thyroxine.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange general blood tests (to evaluate anemia, renal and liver function, vitamin levels; thyroid function testing to be considered given history of hypothyroidism).
    - If blood tests are normal, arrange for physical examination and further assessment.
    - Provide follow-up after blood results: patient will be notified by text to book an appointment when results are available.
    - Advise patient to contact service sooner if symptoms worsen.
- Issue 2: Episodic palpitations and shortness of breath (not exertional when walking; prominent in lifts)
  - Assessment: Intermittent palpitations with sensation of breathlessness, not associated with chest pain; episodes reproducible in lifts/enclosed spaces per patient.
  - Plan:
    - Initial evaluation with planned blood tests to look for reversible metabolic causes.
    - Safety advice: if patient develops chest pain, severe palpitations, or other acute cardiorespiratory symptoms, go to the emergency department (A&E) immediately.
    - If symptoms persist after blood tests, further clinical assessment and investigations (e.g., physical exam, ECG) to be arranged as indicated (to be determined based on results).
- Issue 3: Known hypothyroidism with treatment discontinuation
  - Assessment: Patient has a history of underactive thyroid; reports discontinuation of thyroxine since changing doctors; last blood tests not recent.
  - Plan:
    - Include assessment of thyroid status as part of initial blood testing (implied need for thyroid function testing).
    - Review thyroxine use and consider restarting or adjusting treatment after blood results and clinical review.
- General plan / administrative:
  - Patient to call the support number in the app (03xx number referenced) to arrange blood tests; clinician will complete necessary forms.
  - Results will prompt a text message instructing the patient to book follow-up.
  - Safety netting: seek immediate care for chest pain, severe palpitations, significant change in bowel habits, or vomiting.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Complete current medication list and doses: only thyroxine mentioned; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, temperature, oxygen saturation): not documented.
  - Physical examination findings: not performed / not documented.
  - Exact blood tests to be sent (specific assays and labs) were not fully specified in the transcript.
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use history: not documented.
  - Family medical history: not documented.
  - ECG or other cardiac investigations: not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Timeline conflict: patient reports decreased appetite starting ~3–3.5 months ago after changing jobs, but weight loss is described as starting earlier (approximately 6 months) — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall audible and understandable with occasional interruptions and brief inaudible segments; some patient responses were fragmented. Clinical content sufficient to plan initial investigations but lacks certain standard history elements (allergies, vitals, medication doses).
